# mistershell_tree_element (Data Source)

Reads MisterShell tree_element through the authenticated API. Permissions and scope are enforced by the server.

Requires MisterShell >= 2.1.0.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "mistershell_tree_element" "example" {
  id = "123"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) Numeric element ID.

### Read-Only

- `metadata` (Dynamic) Element from the scoped browse tree including parent_key, element_type, label and config.

## Tree presentation settings

| Field | Valid values |
|---|---|
| `element_type` | `line`, `label` |
| `parent_key` | `location:<positive ID>`, or omitted for root |
| `config.variant` | `badge`, `text` |
| `config.icon` | `label`, `flag`, `star`, `bookmark`, `folder_special`, `dns`, `cloud`, `warning`, `bolt`, `lan`, `hub`, `router`, `storage`, `shield`, `groups` |
| `config.color` | `primary`, `secondary`, `positive`, `negative`, `warning`, `info`, `purple`, `teal`, `indigo`, `orange`, `grey-7` |

All configuration keys are optional. Pass a native Terraform object, without
`jsonencode`. Omitted configuration is null; label elements render as badges
when no variant is selected. Elements are presentation only: they contain no
resources and grant no access. The provider manages type, parent, label and
configuration; sibling ordering is not owned.

Requires `app.resources.read` for the scoped browse tree, plus
`app.resources.write` and `app.resources.delete` for resource management on the
parent location. Root elements require unrestricted location scope. A missing
entry is an error, because tree filtering cannot distinguish deletion from
lost permission. Restore access, or confirm deletion and remove it from
Terraform state before recreating it.

`metadata` is the selected browse node, including `id`, `kind`, `key`,
`parent_key`, `label`, `element_type`, `config`, and presentation flags.
